# Seascape Similarity Analysis

This R Markdown script calculates and visualizes the pairwise similarity between different seascape meta-communities based on plankton counts. It allows users to dynamically toggle between analyzing zooplankton or phytoplankton assemblages.

**Primary Workflows:**

* Aggregate plankton count data into representative meta-communities for each 8-day seascape class.
* Calculate the Chao-Jaccard (abundance-based) similarity index for all unique seascape pairs.
* Apply a masking function to filter duplicate or lower-triangle values for cleaner visualization.
* Render a publication-ready pairwise similarity heatmap comparing seascape classes.

**Required Input Files & Directories:**

* `TS.Master`: *.txt classification files.
* `ctd_meta_v4.csv`: Cruise CTD sampling events and data.

**Environment Requirements & Dependencies:**

* **Data Manipulation & Formatting:** `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `tidyverse`, `lubridate`
* **Visualization:** `ggplot2`

**Author:** E. Montes (enrique.montes@noaa.gov)

**Date:** November 5th, 2025

# Load data files
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

# specify the directory where the files are located
dir_path <- "TS.Master"

# obtain a list of file names in the directory
file_names <- list.files(path = dir_path, pattern = ".txt", full.names = TRUE)

# loop over each file and import the tables (use this for DATES)
for (file in file_names) {
  table_name <- gsub(".txt", "", basename(file)) # get the name of the table from the file name
  assign(table_name, read.table(file = file, header = FALSE, sep = "\t") %>%
           mutate(date = as.POSIXct(substr(V1, start = 24, stop = 36), format="%Y%m%d_%H%M", tz="UTC")))
}

```

# Match file name to cruise data using DATE 
```{r}
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)

dir_path2 <- "cruise_ctd"
file_name <- list.files(path = dir_path2, pattern = "ctd_meta_v4.csv", full.names = TRUE)
ctd_meta <- read.csv(file_name, fill = TRUE)

# Parse dt_list securely and concisely
dt_list <- as.POSIXct(
  sprintf("%04d%02d%02d %s", ctd_meta$year, ctd_meta$month, ctd_meta$day, ctd_meta$time_gmt),
  format = "%Y%m%d %I:%M:%S %p", 
  tz = "UTC"
)

################################################################################
# Detect short transit times between stations
################################################################################
# Vectorized difference calculation in mins
time_differences_mins <- as.numeric(diff(dt_list), units = "mins")

time_diff_df <- data.frame(
  start_time = dt_list[-length(dt_list)],
  end_time = dt_list[-1],
  time_difference_mins = time_differences_mins
)

# CTD time stamps of consecutive stations within less than 20 min
short_timestamps <- dt_list[which(time_differences_mins < 20)]

################################################################################
# Match CPICS records to CTD times & Check unaccounted records
################################################################################
class_names <- c("Acantharea", "Centric", "Ceratium", "Chaetoceros", "Chaetognaths", 
                 "Chain2", "Chain3", "Ostracods", "Copepods", "Decapods", "Echinoderms", 
                 "Guinardia", "Jellies", "Larvaceans", "Neocalyptrella", "Noctiluca", 
                 "pellets", "Polychaets", "Pteropods", "Tricho")

date_limit <- as.POSIXct("2024-11-30", tz = "UTC")
buffer_sec <- 10 * 60 

# Pre-calculate start and end intervals for fast vectorized comparisons
interval_start <- dt_list - buffer_sec
interval_end <- c(dt_list[-1] - buffer_sec, date_limit + 1)

# Process classes in a single pass
results <- setNames(lapply(class_names, function(cname) {
  
  # Fetch ALL data to ensure no unaccounted records slip by
  dts_all <- get(paste0("class.", cname))$date
  
  counts <- integer(length(dt_list))
  accounted <- logical(length(dts_all)) # Tracks if a date falls into any interval
  
  # Check all dates against intervals
  for (i in seq_along(dt_list)) {
    idx <- dts_all >= interval_start[i] & dts_all < interval_end[i]
    counts[i] <- sum(idx & dts_all <= date_limit) # Apply date_limit ONLY to the final count
    accounted[idx] <- TRUE
  }
  
  list(counts = counts, unaccounted = dts_all[!accounted])
  
}), class_names)

# Assemble the final concentration dataframe efficiently
conc_occ_final <- data.frame(date = dt_list)
for (cname in class_names) conc_occ_final[[cname]] <- results[[cname]]$counts

# Combine with metadata and calculate volume
taxa_meta <- cbind(ctd_meta, conc_occ_final) %>%
  mutate(
    sampled_vol_per_min = max(sampled_vol_per_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_vol_sampled = sampled_vol_per_min * conc_deployDurMin
  )

################################################################################
# Output Unaccounted Records & Summary Stats
################################################################################
# Print unaccounted dates per class
for (cname in class_names) {
  cat("Unaccounted dates for class:", cname, "\n")
  print(results[[cname]]$unaccounted)
  cat("\n")
}

# Pre-calculate boolean vectors to simplify stat logic
has_vol <- !is.na(taxa_meta$total_vol_sampled)
has_seascape <- !is.na(taxa_meta$X8.day.seascapes)

sampling_events_img <- sum(has_vol)
seascape_total <- sum(has_seascape)
seascape_match <- sum(has_seascape & has_vol)
total_casts <- nrow(taxa_meta)
percent_match <- round((seascape_match / sampling_events_img) * 100, 0)

# Calculates number of stations occupied during each cruise
station_num_per_cruise <- tapply(taxa_meta$Station, taxa_meta$cruiseID, function(x) length(unique(x)))

# Print stats
cat("Total number CTD casts:", total_casts, "\n")
cat("Percent of CTD casts with seascape match:", round((seascape_total / total_casts) * 100, 0), "%\n")
cat("Percent of CTD casts with images (image profiles):", round((sampling_events_img / total_casts) * 100, 0), "%\n")
cat("Percent of image profiles matched to seascapes:", percent_match, "%\n\n")

print(as.table(station_num_per_cruise))
```

# Calculate Pairwise Seascape Similarity (Figure 8)
```{R}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Define toggle groups
zooplankton <- c("Acantharea", "Chaetognaths", "Ostracods", "Copepods", "Decapods", 
                 "Echinoderms", "Jellies", "Larvaceans", "Polychaets", "Pteropods")
phytoplankton <- c("Centric", "Ceratium", "Chaetoceros", "Chain2", "Chain3", 
                   "Guinardia", "Neocalyptrella", "Noctiluca", "Tricho")
meta_cols <- c("Station", "year", "month", "X8.day.seascapes", "focus_threshold", 
               "sampled_vol_per_min", "total_vol_sampled")

# 2. SET YOUR TOGGLE HERE: Change to either 'zooplankton' or 'phytoplankton'
target_taxa <- phytoplankton 

# 3. Format data and calculate community abundance
c_mh_long <- taxa_meta %>%
  # Select metadata and the target taxa dynamically
  select(all_of(meta_cols), all_of(target_taxa)) %>%
  # Ensure the target taxa columns are formatted properly
  mutate(across(all_of(target_taxa), as.numeric)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(total_vol_sampled) & !is.na(X8.day.seascapes)) %>%
  # Pivot only the selected target taxa
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(target_taxa),
               names_to = "species", values_to = "species_concentration")

seascape_meta_communities <- c_mh_long %>%
  group_by(X8.day.seascapes, species) %>%
  summarise(abundance = sum(species_concentration, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  filter(abundance > 0)

# 4. Nest communities and generate pairwise combinations
nested_seascapes <- seascape_meta_communities %>%
  group_by(X8.day.seascapes) %>%
  nest(community_data = -X8.day.seascapes)

seascape_pairs <- nested_seascapes %>%
  select(seascape_1 = X8.day.seascapes, data_1 = community_data) %>%
  crossing(
    nested_seascapes %>%
      select(seascape_2 = X8.day.seascapes, data_2 = community_data)
  )

# 5. Define Chao-Jaccard calculation function
calculate_chao_jaccard <- function(df1, df2) {
  combined <- full_join(df1, df2, by = "species", suffix = c("_1", "_2")) %>%
    mutate(
      abundance_1 = replace_na(abundance_1, 0),
      abundance_2 = replace_na(abundance_2, 0)
    )
  n <- sum(combined$abundance_1)
  m <- sum(combined$abundance_2)
  if (n == 0 || m == 0) return(NA_real_)

  p_i <- combined$abundance_1 / n
  q_i <- combined$abundance_2 / m

  sum_of_mins <- sum(pmin(p_i, q_i))
  sum_of_maxs <- sum(pmax(p_i, q_i))

  return(sum_of_mins / sum_of_maxs)
}

# 6. Calculate similarities and mask duplicate/lower triangle values
pairwise_similarity_updated <- seascape_pairs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(C_J = calculate_chao_jaccard(data_1, data_2)) %>%
  select(seascape_1, seascape_2, C_J) %>%
  mutate(
    C_J = if_else(
      as.numeric(as.character(seascape_2)) < as.numeric(as.character(seascape_1)),
      NA_real_,
      C_J
    )
  )

# 7. Render Final Heatmap
pairwise_similarity_updated$seascape_1 <- factor(pairwise_similarity_updated$seascape_1,
                                   levels = c(3, 11, 13, 15, 21, 27),
                                   labels = c("TST", "TSU", "SGMI", "TS", "WBHN", "HE"))
pairwise_similarity_updated$seascape_2 <- factor(pairwise_similarity_updated$seascape_2,
                                   levels = c(3, 11, 13, 15, 21, 27),
                                   labels = c("TST", "TSU", "SGMI", "TS", "WBHN", "HE"))

similarity_hm <- ggplot(pairwise_similarity_updated, aes(x = seascape_1, y = seascape_2, fill = C_J)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(C_J, 2)), color = "black", size = 8) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#fee8c8", 
    high = "#006400", # b30000 for zooplankton / 006400 for phyto
    name = "Similarity", 
    limit = c(0.21,1),
    breaks = seq(0.2, 1.0, by = 0.2)) +  
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 32, angle = 0, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 32, angle = 0, color = "black"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 18),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 22, margin = margin(b = 15)))

print(similarity_hm)
```
